layout: Give each spread one governing composition rather than repeating a card grid everywhere.
Use a persistent folio and issue system, then permit controlled exceptions for full-bleed pages.
Treat density as a deliberate mode: POPEYE-like catalog pages can be dense, while Gentlewoman-like profiles need air.
Show the book as a physical object only when spine, top edge, thickness, and light make the pose legible.
Keep a stable navigational grammar while each scroll chapter changes its evidence, as Prime Intellect does with numbered anchors and figure labels.
Organize publication archives by issue and year so the cover sequence reads as a body of work rather than an undifferentiated feed.
imagery: Prefer a single commissioned-feeling idea on the cover over several equal-weight promotional lines.
Use real personal photography as editorial material, not as generic card thumbnails.
Let typography become the image on concept-led pages; avoid adding decoration merely to fill space.
iconography: Use print furniture—folios, issue marks, rules, barcodes, running heads—as functional system elements.
Keep UI icons subordinate to the publication object.
motion: Name the verb and its trigger before animating: enter, settle, turn, gather, preview, zoom, or morph—caused by load, scroll, hover, cursor, or selection.
Use scroll to mark chapters and change reading mode, not to apply constant parallax to every surface.
Let hover disclose a useful preview or alternate state; do not animate solely to prove that an element is interactive.
Give cursor-reactive work a legible consequence, such as gathering a form or changing the camera—not an ambient wobble.
Preserve origin and destination during layout transitions, following Studio K95's Rings-to-Spiral morph instead of teleporting items.
Use one memorable interaction per spread and keep metadata, marginalia, and secondary controls on a quieter tempo.
Honor reduced-motion preferences with still poster frames, direct state changes, and skippable entrances.
avoid: Do not copy the palette of any source; the project stays white, near-black, and one red.
Do not borrow mymind's gradient language or the first version's beige editorial styling.
Do not imitate covers literally or republish source artwork.
Do not make every spread equally sparse or equally dense.
Do not use a 3D pose that reads as a flat rectangle rotated in space.
Do not infer a site's behavior from an aggregate thumbnail when the live site can be observed.
Do not trap the reader behind a long logo-only loader.
Do not publish screenshots or media from Alan's private mymind space.

composition_ideas: Object-first issue reveal inspired by Stripe Press product presentation.
Conceptual cover-title build followed by quiet folio metadata.
Alternation between dense POPEYE-like catalogs and airy Gentlewoman-like profiles.
A stable numbered chapter rail whose surrounding evidence changes from cover to spread to archive.
A cover archive that can morph between chronological shelf, thematic cluster, and selected-issue focus while preserving object identity.

remotion.lower_third: Server Mono issue metadata with a single hairline; no rounded container.
